plan.title: Liver drug treatment DE (3v3) + power caveat + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq from human liver, salmon-derived gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 6 samples (3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch). With n=3 per group the design has real but limited power: DESeq2/edgeR at 3 replicates recover only a minority of true DE genes, biased toward large effect sizes, so absence from the significant list is not evidence of no change. The plan follows the DESeq2-anchored bulk RNA-seq procedure returned by the knowledge service (grounded, digest sha256:709bb1f7...): sample-structure QC before any test, minimal count pre-filtering, DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization with the negative binomial Wald test plus apeglm shrinkage, an edgeR quasi-likelihood run for cross-method robustness (intersection = high-confidence set), BH-FDR with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and preranked fgsea (ranked on the Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets (both confirmed staged for human, 2026.1/current releases) rather than an over-representation test, since the small n makes an ORA on a short significant list underpowered. Every report step states the replicate count, expected power, and reproducibility record explicitly, per the flagged low-power design rule.

fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column), full ranked gene list (no threshold), tested against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets then Reactome pathway gene sets as a second collection
